hebdo.accroche: A sweeping Democratic victory in the US midterm elections has disrupted Washington's political landscape, already triggering shifts in strategic aid and trade policy. Simultaneously, the global air and missile defence arena saw major developments, marked by North Korean and Iranian missile escalations, tactical laser demonstrations, and European rearmament contracts.

tendances.titre: Intensifying missile developments and high-end air defence recapitalisation
tendances.resume: Ballistic and cruise missile capabilities are advancing rapidly, with North Korea testing cruise missile dispersal warheads alongside a new SAM system resembling the S-400. Tehran announced the removal of self-imposed missile range limits while exploring Russian S-400 acquisitions. In response, European and allied nations are heavily expanding surface-to-air inventories, including France doubling Aster 30 loads on FDI frigates and the US accelerating AMRAAM and Standard Missile production.

tendances.titre: Acceleration of counter-UAS systems and directed-energy weapons
tendances.resume: Armed forces worldwide are moving urgently to operationalise low-cost kinetic and directed-energy counter-drone solutions. Hanwha Systems demonstrated successful drone intercepts using a 30kW laser, whilst the US deployed LOCUST laser systems domestically and delivered 25,000 C-UAS assets to CENTCOM. In Europe, France advanced its LADAC laser-guided rocket programme to counter uncrewed aerial systems economically.

tendances.titre: US midterm political shift creates geopolitical and defence friction
tendances.resume: A historic Democratic sweep of Congress in the US midterms has triggered domestic political realignment and sharp tech sector volatility. The political fallout coincides with abrupt White House foreign policy manoeuvres, notably the announced termination of annual military assistance to Israel. Despite political friction in Washington, core Indo-Pacific commitments remain steady, with Taiwan confirming uninterrupted arms sales and taking delivery of its first F-16 Block 70 fighters.

tendances.titre: Middle East naval flashpoints compel Indo-Pacific operational responses
tendances.resume: Targeted US military strikes against Iranian radar and missile facilities on Qeshm Island and an expanded trade blockade have heightened maritime risks across the Strait of Hormuz. Asian states reliant on these vital sea lines of communication are taking direct protective measures. South Korea deployed maritime patrol and mine-countermeasure assets to the Gulf, whilst Singapore emphasised at the Manama Dialogue that maritime waterway insecurity cannot become the status quo.

tendances.titre: Hardening defence postures and deterrence initiatives across Asia-Pacific
tendances.resume: Indo-Pacific nations are modernising tactical dispersed footprints and coastal strike networks to deter regional coercion. The Philippines confirmed dispersed joint basing with the US and progressed BrahMos anti-ship missile acquisitions, while Japan deployed Type 16 combat vehicles to the Nansei Islands. Naval modernisation also progressed with South Korea launching its second KSS-III Batch-II submarine, alongside stepped-up bilateral air patrols between Singapore and Indonesia.

tendances.titre: Hybrid disruptions exploit civilian infrastructure and emergency networks
tendances.resume: Coordinated cyber intrusions and grey-zone disruptions increasingly targeted civilian and emergency infrastructure. Air raid alert applications in Ukraine and Russia were hijacked by hackers to broadcast fabricated nuclear warnings. Meanwhile, industrial control hacks on European cold-chain networks prompted warnings from Singapore's Cyber Security Agency, and waves of coordinated hoax bomb threats disrupted European aviation.
